subjects.what: The kernel's own video console writing to the frame buffer in emulation: the frame buffer dump after BSD initialisation holds 3,795 bright pixels in a monospaced text pattern on a black 800x600 panel

subjects.limits: One boot, one photograph. It proves the panel takes our writes at these coordinates and that the firmware reports this mode; it says nothing about the kernel, which is loaded later in the chain.

subjects.what: Both a staged kernel with the new post-MMU bar and the previous staged kernel panic in the emulator at fipspost_post_integrity (-74), so staging, not this round's injection, breaks the crypto POST
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only, and it says nothing about the handset except this: the image this port stages for the phone is not the image CI validates, and it fails the kernel's own integrity POST before bsd_init.

subjects.what: The post-MMU bring-up bar drawn through the kernel console's own panel mapping: at bsd_init the instrument reports vinfo base=fffffff04f604000 row=3200 height=600 with the full command line, and paints 12,800 pixels of the bottom 16 rows while leaving the two bootstrap bars off
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only, 800x600. It proves the instrument, its mapping and its switch on this panel size; the handset panel is 1080x1920 with a different stride, and the pixels there are still the open question.

subjects.what: NativeSdhci built as a loadable kext bundle and packed into an mkext container on the macOS runner: an arm64 MH_KEXT_BUNDLE with 645 symbols and the kmod record, packed as a 95,462-byte mkext2 with its info dictionaries page-aligned at 94,208
subjects.label: ABI-compiled
subjects.limits: Built and structurally checked; never loaded by a kernel yet. The kernel-side call to OSKext::loadFromMkext() is the next step, and nothing here says it will succeed.

subjects.what: The merged (prelinked) image panics on the assertion '!prng_ready' after IOKit entry, because both the source crypto bootstrap patch and the prelinked Apple corecrypto initialize the PRNG
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only. It names the panic precisely; the fix belongs to the framework patch that runs the source crypto bootstrap, not to this port's drivers.

subjects.what: The merged (prelinked) image now passes arm_vm_init, the source crypto bootstrap, PE_init_iokit and reaches bsd_init, stopping on 'Failed to mount root device' -- the root-device wait this whole objective is about
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only. It proves the merged image reaches BSD initialisation; the root device it waits for is the next piece of work, not a property of this run.

subjects.what: The storage driver's 95,462-byte mkext container is embedded in the kernel image and reachable at runtime: a boot with the lumia-kext switch reports the container's size from inside the kernel
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only, and the load itself does not happen: OSKext::loadFromMkext() is private at this pin, so the kernel reports the container and stops there. What is proven is the embedding and the call site, not a load.

subjects.what: The kernel's prelink loader reads an entry that this repository inserted into a merged image: it reports 'Kext org.unixnu.NativeSdhci error - CFBundleVersion missing/invalid type'
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only. It proves the edit reaches the kernel's kext loader and that the loader validates the fields; placing a real executable at a real address is the remaining work.

subjects.what: The prelink loader validates an entry's fields in order -- bundle id/version, then the kmod_info address, then uses it -- as shown by three successive boots whose complaints advance and then stop
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only, and the last boot faults because the address points at kernel text on purpose. It shows the entry schema is accepted; it does not show a kext loading.

subjects.what: The kext container was extracted from the kernel image, its executable placed at a chosen address with a new segment, and described to the loader; the boot then faults inside _mach_vm_allocate_kernel, so the address choice and the missing symbol binding are the next two problems
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only, and it is a negative result: the placement does not load. It pins the failure to the kernel's own allocation step, which is progress against 'the entry is not read at all'.

subjects.what: With the kext placed by a new segment, the boot faults inside _mach_vm_allocate_kernel at a fault_far that differs on every boot -- the signature of the kernel's slide not being applied to the added segment the way the emitter's segments are
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only, and a negative result. The earlier placement runs are superseded: they used a merged image built before the PRNG guard, which is recorded in the note.

subjects.what: Growing a mapped segment to hold the kext is implemented and its output is read by the loader, which refuses it with 'overlapping virtual segments' because the chosen segment ends where the next one begins
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only. The refusal is a real load of a real image by the real loader: it proves the edit chain works and names the geometry constraint; it is not a loaded kext.

subjects.what: The exact files deployed on the handset -- loader 94,208 B, the UniXNU tree with DarwinBoot.efi, and kernel 7ae95f48 with args '-v cpus=1 lumia-bars2' -- reach bsd_init in emulation and paint the 12,800-pixel bottom bar
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only. It proves the deployed bytes are sound; it does not prove the handset executes them, which is what the bottom-bar photograph is for.

subjects.what: The post-MMU progress instrument masked DAIF and never restored it, so the first allocation after the bar panicked with 'Calling {k,z}alloc from interrupt disabled context isn't allowed'; the instrument now saves and restores DAIF and a source test holds that invariant
subjects.label: host-tested
subjects.limits: The panic was observed in emulation; what is verified here is the source invariant and that the component still compiles for aarch64 in preflight. The fix itself has not been booted yet.

subjects.what: With DAIF saved and restored, the kernel no longer panics after painting the bar: it proceeds into dlil_init and skmem_region_init and the bottom bar is still 12,800 pixels
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only. The kernel that was deployed to the handset is this build (3b65f550), so the next hardware boot exercises the fix, but that boot has not happened.

subjects.what: The three files now on the handset -- loader 9d9311b3, config with skmem_sysctl_skip=1, kernel 3b65f550 -- boot in emulation through IOKit into bsd_init, paint the 12,800-pixel bottom bar and stop on 'Failed to mount root device'
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only. It is the best configuration this repository knows how to produce; whether the handset executes it is still the open question.

subjects.limits: Emulator only, but it is a measurement of the kernel's own structure at a named instruction, so it carries to any platform that runs this kernel: the ordering is in the source, not in the emulator.

subjects.what: A read-only audit of the working handset chain and of the MainOS question: the file inventory with the values measured this session, the three records that disagree with the phone (CRITICAL hashes, the EFIESP image size and hash, the BCD size), the absence of any per-file inventory of the unlock patches, and why formatting MainOS is not a recoverable step
subjects.label: source-reviewed
subjects.limits: Documentation and repository records only. The values quoted from the handset were read earlier in this session while the phone was in mass storage mode; the phone is now disconnected, so nothing was re-measured for this audit.

subjects.what: The six protected boot-chain object classes are enforced in code: scripts/boot-chain-guard.py decides, phone-install.py refuses an existing protected replacement without --replace-protected, and tests hold both the rule and the wiring
subjects.label: host-tested
subjects.limits: Host tests only: they exercise the guard and the scripts against temporary volumes. Nothing here was run against the phone, and no protected object was written.

subjects.what: One shared decision point (scripts/boot-chain-io.py) now governs replacing and deleting the six protected boot-chain classes, with --replace-protected/--delete-protected plus an existing backup, a reason and a verification plan; the installer, the updater and the snapshot restore all go through it, and tests cover the incomplete-request refusals
subjects.label: host-tested
subjects.limits: Host tests against temporary volumes. No phone was connected and no protected object was written; the microSD experiment is still a design with unverified capabilities.

subjects.what: The objective is restated as five non-skippable milestones on the handset: M1 BSD initialisation, M2 eMMC controller and block device, M3 read-only GPT, M4 APFS container and volumes, M5 APFS root and userland; the microSD experiment is auxiliary and MainOS formatting is not a prerequisite. Read-only access is enforced in the storage driver and held by a test
subjects.label: host-tested
subjects.limits: The milestone definition is written material; the part measured here is the read-only guard, which is host-tested. M1 itself is unmet and every milestone's evidence column names the handset as the judge.

subjects.what: Two additional skip switches (wfe_timeout_* and kernel_startup_bootstrap) were measured to break the emulated boot even with both switched off: four configurations stop at _sleh_synchronous_sp1 while the same tree without them reaches root-wait, so they were withdrawn and the bisect stays at the five verified calls
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator only. It is a negative result about an instrument, not about the handset: nothing here says anything about how far the kernel gets on the phone.

subjects.what: Six forms on one artifact with the self-test running the handset's own geometry (stride 4320, width 1080, rows 8..15): the plain marker draws (state 0), the dry form maps without drawing (1), the self-test takes the handset's existing-table branch with its sentinels intact (30), and the untouched configuration reports 4 -- all reaching root-wait with ESR 0x0
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: QEMU only. The handset has not run this kernel: its branch and its numbers are exercised, its hardware is not.

subjects.what: The early marker row range and block indices are checked arithmetically for both panels — Lumia (1080x1920, stride 4320, video base 0x400000) and the QEMU fixture — so every store of the range lands inside the 2 MB block the marker maps
subjects.label: host-tested
subjects.limits: Arithmetic and source only: the handset has not run this kernel, and the handset branch (an existing gigabyte entry, so only a leaf entry is added) has not been executed anywhere yet.

subjects.what: The handset deployment of the early-map kernel is a script with guards: artifact hash, chain presence, a kept copy of the replaced kernel, and the boot-chain gate; a dry run writes nothing and the boot argument is added once
subjects.label: host-tested
subjects.limits: Host tests against temporary volumes. The script has not run against the phone, because the phone is not connected.

subjects.what: The early marker decision branches are modelled and tested exhaustively on the host: empty gigabyte, existing table (the handset case), covering block, non-covering block, taken leaf slot, same block, zero address, and the row range that used to cross the block boundary
subjects.label: host-tested
subjects.limits: A model of the C, not the C: it catches logic errors in the branch table, not drift between the model and the kernel. The C remains the authority.

subjects.what: A strict read-only GPT reader with a synthetic fixture: protective MBR, header and entry-array CRCs, primary/backup agreement and overlap checks, with four corruption modes each refused for its own reason
subjects.label: host-tested
subjects.limits: The fixture is synthetic -- names and LBAs are declared, not read from any device. This is the reference the kernel side of M3 has to match, not evidence about the handset GPT.

subjects.what: The kernel-side read-only GPT parser (drivers/Common/GptRead.c) compiles clean with -Wall -Wextra -Werror, cross-compiles for arm64, and agrees field by field with the Python reference reader on the same synthetic image, refusing the same four corruptions for the same reasons
subjects.label: ABI-compiled
subjects.limits: Host compilation, an arm64 cross-compile and a synthetic image. The parser has not been linked into XNU and no real disk has been read, so neither kernel-linked nor hardware-tested is claimed.

subjects.what: The GPT parser runs inside the kernel against a synthetic disk and reports 0: it accepted a valid table with the partition it wrote (EFI, 64..200) and refused a header-CRC-damaged one for that reason, on the same artifact where all six early-marker forms still reach root-wait
subjects.label: kernel-linked
subjects.limits: A synthetic disk in memory. The parser has not read a real disk, so hardware-tested is not claimed and no real GPT has been parsed.

subjects.what: A six-step M2 integration plan with a decision rule for kext delivery (prelink injection first), per-step pass/fail criteria, and the two steps that make the read-only guarantee measurable (read one sector, and prove no write command was issued)
subjects.label: host-tested
subjects.limits: A plan. No kext is bundled, nothing is injected into the prelinked image, and the read-only proof is still source-level: measured only by tests on the driver sources.

subjects.what: The NativeSdhci kext and its mkext container are built in the kernel job before the archive that embeds them, and checked on the runner: an arm64 kext bundle with 645 symbols and five segments, a 95,462-byte container whose plist sits at 94,208 with checksum 0x4AEB457C, and no archive-step failure anywhere in the build
subjects.label: kernel-linked
subjects.limits: The bundle and container are built and validated, not delivered: M2's S2 (putting it into the prelinked image) is still refused, and nothing has run against the device

subjects.what: The storage driver counts every command it issues, counts write and erase opcodes separately, and refuses a write before the command register is touched, so M2's read-only guarantee (S6) can be measured at run time instead of read off the source
subjects.label: ABI-compiled
subjects.limits: Instrumentation only: the counters are compiled for arm64 and checked by source tests, but the driver does not run yet, so no counter has ever been read at run time

subjects.what: Reading the prelink tool shows why a hand-appended kext entry is refused: components are discovered from the image own plist, their code must be backed by the image segments, and their extents may not overlap -- so S2 needs a layout slot, not another injector
subjects.label: source-reviewed
subjects.limits: A reading of the prelink tool source, not a run of it: no merge was attempted locally, and the two candidate routes (framework manifest change, loader delivery) are both unstarted.

subjects.what: The polling layer of the storage driver (PollingHost, SdhciCore) includes no IOKit headers, so it can be compiled into the image through the same channel as the GPT parser -- a third route that could reach real eMMC reads before kext delivery is solved, but not IOMedia publication
subjects.label: source-reviewed
subjects.limits: A source-level observation and a documented route. Route C is not started: it cannot be validated in QEMU, its power/clock sequencing is unknown, and it would not satisfy the IOMedia part of M2.

subjects.what: The SDHCI identification probe executes in QEMU when its boot argument is present: the boot reaches the VM return, the marker and the GPT self-check, then faults on the first read of the SDHCI window (ESR 0x96000010 at the mapped KVA); without the argument all six marker forms still reach root-wait
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: QEMU has no SDHCI controller, so this measures the probe's wiring and the mapping, not the controller. No register has been read from real hardware.

subjects.what: The handset deployment procedure was rehearsed end to end on a copy of the staged EFIESP tree: the dry run wrote nothing, apply wrote the artifact, kept the previous kernel in the backup, appended the boot argument once, passed the boot-chain gate and wrote the runbook
subjects.label: host-tested
subjects.limits: A copy of the staged tree, not the phone: no handset file was touched and no boot was performed

subjects.what: The storage driver runs against a host register model of the SDHCI controller and is accepted, in both shapes: a cold command sequence (CMD0..CMD3, CMD17 reading 512 bytes that match the pattern, 512 reported) and the warm path the phone actually takes (WarmCard::attach finding an RCA, deselecting, decoding the CSD and EXT_CSD, selecting again and reading a block), with zero write or erase commands in either
subjects.label: host-tested
subjects.limits: A model of the controller, not the controller: it proves the driver's sequences are legal for this model, and says nothing about the Lumia's SDHCI window, clock or card

subjects.what: The driver encoded the SDHCI command register as (index << 8) | flags, which matches the reference implementation in EDK2 SdMmcPciHci.c: index shifted into bits 8..13, BIT1|BIT3|BIT4 for R1/R5/R6/R7, BIT0|BIT3 for R2, BIT5 for data present; the register model follows that encoding
subjects.label: host-tested
subjects.limits: Compared against a published reference implementation, not against the controller: the encoding is right, the registers still have not answered on the phone

subjects.what: The GPT parser reads its sectors through the storage driver's warm-card path against the register model: the parser accepts the synthetic table, reports both partitions, the EFI/SYSTEM and Microsoft types and their extents, and the whole read issues no write or erase command -- the same interface M3 needs on the phone
subjects.label: host-tested
subjects.limits: The sectors come from a model of the controller, not from eMMC: this proves the interface between the driver and the parser, not that the handset's disk can be read

subjects.what: Three sweeps of the six marker forms on one artifact -- eighteen boots -- produce identical results: off 4, dry 1, draw 0, noclean 0, notlbi 0, selftest 30, every one reaching root-wait with ESR 0x0
subjects.label: QEMU-tested
subjects.limits: Emulator repeatability on one artifact. It says the instrument is deterministic where it has run; it says nothing about the handset, which has never run this kernel
